eventFormat.comment: Durable task-event payload format version, stamped into every persisted storage_events/storage_attempt_events row at the single write authority (compile_event_item). Readers refuse a payload whose envelope version is newer than the binary understands AND is not marked ignorable; an ignorable newer payload is skipped, never silently resumed. Bump only on semantic unreadability.

physicalRules: Entity B+Tree order is tenant ID, owner ID, physical namespace, then raw key bytes; key length never precedes key content.

Every authority commit carries a tri-state entity-root update in its v2 transaction envelope and publishes the resulting current root in checksummed CONTROL; normal entity open verifies that CONTROL root without reading history, while legacy slots use one exact bounded transaction lookup.

Every live entity transaction pins its immutable MVCC root in a database-instance registry; handles have no count admission quota, release is tied to handle lifetime, and handles cannot cross reopen boundaries.
Entity transactions retain all distinct point and range witnesses needed for OCC without a witness-count admission quota; repeated point reads reuse their existing witness.

The per-open entity transaction registry accounts actual retained bytes across point witnesses, worst-case range witnesses, and staged writes without an aggregate admission quota; arithmetic overflow fails closed and reservations release with transaction lifetime.

Normal entity open reads and verifies only the content-addressed current root node; fully materialized roots without restored ranges remain direct B+Tree pages; partial materialization uses a version-2 directory with exact WAL coverage, while a versioned directory may overlay at most 64 sorted non-overlapping capsule range mounts on one base root. Descendant pages are verified lazily, base records and tombstones override mounted values, writes COW only the base, and one transaction may retire at most 64 sorted non-overlapping ranges or change mounts under an exact root witness. Explicit lazy consolidation materializes at most 999 rows and 8388608 bytes per commit by atomically replacing a mounted prefix in the base; it never runs during open and eventually collapses an exhausted directory to its direct base root.

Explicit entity reachability walks are streaming and reject level or key-range transplants without a database-sized visited set; they admit at most 20000000 pages and an 8192-node frontier, follow root-directory bases and mounts plus at most 1000000 authority-global monotonic persistent full roots or 64-range capsules declared by the current CONTROL root, and require the discovered pin count to equal its transactional catalog. Catalogued pin admission uses bounded point reads; an absent catalog may upgrade at most 64 legacy pins.

Explicit backup and garbage-collection reachability follows persisted stream segment references plus blob-backed versioned-document, command-receipt, and logical-outbox leaf values as owner-bound semantic graph edges without consulting transaction history; ordinary open and foreground range retirement do not scan values.

Stream cursors and immutable segment references live in the current entity root alongside retained-prefix watermarks; metadata v2 decodes legacy v1 with a retained base of one, normal authority open never rebuilds catalogs from historical commits, retired cursors fail explicitly, and reads resolve at most 1000 events and 8 MiB from the caller's MVCC snapshot.

Automatic history maintenance retains at most 64 complete immutable 4 MiB segments through a suffix-only v2 manifest, never rewrites transaction payloads or checkpoints an active WAL, and publishes only after one launch-probed low-priority maintenance admission.

Explicit authority garbage collection first stream-matches at most 20000000 loose-directory entries with constant retained memory and removes at most one strictly named bounded .new temporary block file before reachability marking. It then streams current Entity, persistent capsule, semantic external-block, retained-history, and active-WAL reachability into bounded on-volume mark runs; it refuses live MVCC handles, republishes unchanged CONTROL state before referenced-file deletion, removes at most 65536 loose blocks or 268435456 bytes, scans at most 4163 payload-segment directory entries (4096 catalog slots + 2 in-flight background publications + 64 deferred retirements + 1) and removes at most one strictly named unreferenced complete or temporary segment, then inspects one generation-selected catalog window of at most 16 manifest segments and rewrites or retires at most one through a double-stabilized catalog per repeatable round. When the selected round has no reclaimable victim, it may compact at least 128 and at most 65536 reachable, not-already-segmented loose blocks in one bounded cross-shard batch within both the 268435456-byte segment ceiling and the launch-derived temporary-space budget; an executed no-victim catalog window advances the durable CONTROL cursor.

rules: Explicit generic entity/document keys must match the transaction tenant and owner at IR validation; only built-in identity-writing steps receive narrowly enumerated tenant-global claim prefixes from the authority interpreter.
Queries cannot contain writes or command effects.

Commands require effects derived from admitted catalog metadata, never client write flags, except turn.perception.record: its sole bounded attempt-document mutation commits without a receipt or logical outbox record.
Receipt lookup precedes semantic effects; new receipt, outbox capture, and business writes commit atomically.
Conditions and result projections may reference only previously initialized bounded slots.

conversation-sync envelopes carry top-level turnId for every Turn-specific change and attemptId for every Attempt-specific change; identity-free aggregate and deletion changes omit both fields

conversation-sync writes maintain an owner-scoped age index and exact Attempt-event reference keys; Attempt age locators retain the identity and sequence evidence needed to remove those references after conversation deletion retires the replay range; turn.sync.prune removes at most 1000 replay rows and 67108864 materialized bytes per transaction, leaves the monotonic head intact, and releases every matching transport-retention fence atomically

large live projections move to one owner-scoped immutable checkpoint plus at most 64 exact revision patches totaling at most 1 MiB; Turn reads reconstruct by bounded point lookups, terminal settlement materializes once, and ordinary open never scans heads

reconstructed projection checkpoints and terminal Turn documents use the bounded Turn snapshot budget, not the transaction literal budget; incoming full projections and patches retain their independent request admission and terminal settlement preserves retained projection content
legacy inline image reads select one of at most 20 images and return at most 8 MiB of base64 source bytes without exporting the surrounding Turn projection
tenant-global identity claim namespaces are writable only by the bounded create/append IR steps and never expose another owner's document
delta synchronization scans an owner/conversation/time revision index before materializing only projections newer than the caller's known revision
delta candidate and tombstone sets are capped at 2000 rows and oversized or over-budget responses fail atomically instead of returning an incomplete view
new lane ordinals are monotonically allocated from zero by an OCC-protected lane-head witness; deletion may leave stable gaps

Turn creation and mutation maintain a compact lane covering index with identity, parent, lifecycle, revision and update-time fields; turn.compact scans at most 100000 such rows and materializes only deletion-closure, anchor, reparented or projection-updated Turn blobs

turn.compact validates at most 2000 combined deletion, reparent and projection-update mutations, with at most 512 reparented Turns, a 67108864-byte materialization ceiling and 512 retained projection updates totaling at most 8388608 bytes, then atomically deletes the folded graph, rewrites retained projections and parents, inserts the summary, advances exact counts and publishes one snapshot-required replay invalidation
lane allocation heads are monotonic while exact live counts are independently maintained so deletions never make paging totals stale
turn and every historical attempt identity claim survive logical deletion in a versioned bounded tombstone until garbage collection so delete and recreate cannot produce an ABA identity

conversation trash capsules retain and restore the bounded attempt identity directory and count but not Attempt documents or events; the inert metadata cannot execute and lets later deletion or permanent purge release every fenced identity
each deleting transaction prunes at most 256 owner-scoped tombstones older than seven days through the age-leading index and releases only ownership-verified identity claims

terminal supersession maintains one owner-scoped age-leading superseded-attempt index in the same transaction as the Attempt document; turn.cleanup scans at most 256 index rows, revalidates the exact superseded status and timestamp, refuses attempts still referenced as a live Turn current attempt or by retained conversation-sync replay data, and atomically removes at most 64 superseded non-current Attempts with their events, derived indexes, exact Turn directory and count repair, and bounded raw-archive state while retaining tenant-global identity claims against delete/recreate ABA
one delete resolves at most 2000 settled turns across at most 256 recursively owned branch lanes before its first write

document, lane/update indexes, counts, every historical attempt and event range, derived attempt indexes, tombstones, conversation header, sync event, outbox, and search invalidation delete atomically

settled projection replacement uses projection-revision CAS and atomically updates the blob-capable document, lane/update indexes, conversation revision, search invalidation, compact replay patch, and outbox

model-context history proofs derive semantic revision from projection revision minus an authority-verified display-only update offset; the private nonnegative offset never exceeds projection revision, remains excluded from public Turn documents, and is preserved by exclusive offline Turn snapshot import/export; missing legacy offset is zero and normal native open never migrates history
turn reads are owner and conversation scoped and never scan projection blobs outside the requested bounded page
activity-date queries scan at most 100000 compact main-lane timestamp records per request and materialize legacy Turn documents only when the complete per-conversation index is absent
projections and settlements are object-valued JSON and overflow to owner-bound blobs

logicalTables.name: plugin_manifests
constraints: manifest identity is the declared namespace scoped to the authenticated tenant and owner
register validates the full manifest before reading state and every validation failure is a typed incompatible rejection
equal versions require byte-identical canonical manifests and lower versions are rejected before any write
higher versions must be append-only: existing columns primary keys indexes and operations survive unchanged and new columns are optional with no new unique index
one bounded document per namespace carries the normalized manifest and commits atomically

logicalTables.name: raw_archives
constraints: archive identity is claimed tenant-globally so a re-put under another owner is a typed conflict while an identical re-put under the claiming owner replays idempotently
put proves the owning attempt row under the same owner with matching conversation turn and task before any write and a missing owner is a typed not-found
compressed part bytes travel inside the put step outside the shared 8 MiB literal pool and each part stays within 16 MiB with the pair within the same 16 MiB per-attempt budget

tenant-global and per-attempt stored-byte counters admit or scrub: budget or free-space exhaustion scrubs to a partial archive with empty parts and reason quota_exhausted and attempt-budget exhaustion scrubs likewise with reason attempt_limit
part bytes ride inside one bounded document per archive that spills to an owner-bound blob so authority GC retains exactly the live archive bytes
list order is (created_at_ms, archive_id) ascending reproduced by task and task+round covering indexes of big-endian timestamp then id, bounded by a 64-row page
reads inflate strictly: a stored part must finish its zlib stream within 64 MiB decoded with no unused trailing bytes, and any violation is a typed integrity error

conversation deletion reads only a compact removal index capped at 512 rows, verifies exact count and stored-byte aggregates and claim ownership, and atomically retires documents, task/round/attempt indexes, usage and global ID claims

logicalTables.name: knowledge_documents
constraints: document identity is owner scoped and the sha256 digest index admits at most one live document per digest so create replays as created=false with the existing metadata
one versioned document per document/chunk/asset spills chunk bodies and enriched text to owner-bound blobs so authority GC retains exactly the live corpus
chunk and asset ordinals are contiguous from zero and every chunk asset reference resolves to a declared asset with a unique (asset, relation) pair

search terms are Python casefolded whitespace tokens deduplicated per chunk and projected into a term-first inverted index whose posting order reproduces the legacy (matched_terms, document_updated_at, document_id, chunk_ordinal) ranking
catalogue filters reproduce legacy semantics exactly: Python casefold on the query, ASCII-only LOWER on stored names and kinds, escaped LIKE containment, and the frozen category CASE mapping
per-owner aggregate counters and category facets count only library and shared documents and move atomically with every create replace delete patch and enrichment status transition
enrichment claims walk a (kind class, created_at, document, ordinal) queue of pending or running assets in library or shared documents and stale running rows become claimable after thirty minutes
the tenant-global enrichment owner index mirrors (visual_enrichment and at least one pending or running library or shared asset) so owner discovery stays bounded
owner clear retires every knowledge entity of the owner including settings counters queue entries and the global owner index witness

materialization.vacuum: preserves mounts and uncovered WAL suffix even when base becomes empty
